newsitem.title: GERMANY: German gold plan may raise 12 bln dmk - govt sources.
newsitem.headline: German gold plan may raise 12 bln dmk - govt sources.

text.p: A plan by Germany to revalue the gold reserves of the Bundesbank could swell federal finances by an extra 10 billion marks to 12 billion marks ($6 billion to $7 billion) in 1997, German government coalition sources said on Tuesday.
A second, similarly-sized inflow of revenue from a gold revaluation could be expected for 1998, the sources added. ($ = 1.693 German Marks)
Government sources said earlier that the Bundesbank was expected on Wednesday to issue a statement outlining its position on a planned higher valuation of its gold reserves.
The sources added that the central bank council had basically accepted the plan for a higher valuation of its gold reserves and would be unlikely to seek to prevent it taking effect in 1997.

Confusion remains however on how, and indeed whether, Bonn could use the measure to cut back its 1997 budget deficit to the three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) required for entry into the single European currency.
